artists.biography: The Wedding Present are a British indie rock group based in Leeds, England, formed in 1985 from the ashes of the Lost Pandas. The band's music has evolved from fast-paced indie rock in the vein of their most obvious influences The Fall, Buzzcocks and Gang of Four to more varied forms. Throughout their career, they have been led by vocalist and guitarist David Gedge, the band's only constant member.

## The Hit Parade

The Wedding Present's 1992 Hit Parade project stands as an audacious conceptual undertaking that redefined the band's commercial and artistic ambitions. Released as a series of twelve limited-edition singles throughout the year—one each month from January through December—the project saw each single feature an original composition on the A-side paired with a carefully curated cover on the B-side. The A-sides represent some of the band's strongest original work, while the B-sides showcase inspired interpretations of songs ranging from Neil Young's "Don't Cry No Tears" to The Monkees' "Pleasant Valley Sunday." The ambitious scope of the undertaking was deliberate: The Wedding Present aimed to match Elvis Presley's 1957 record of twelve top 40 singles in a single year, a feat they successfully achieved.

Following the heavier, guitar-driven aesthetic established on 1991's Seamonsters, the Hit Parade singles maintained the band's evolved sound while showcasing their versatility across both original material and covers. Each single was pressed in a limited edition of 10,000 copies and deleted shortly after release, making them highly collectible. The accompanying picture sleeves featured imaginative designs depicting the numbers 1–12, reinforcing the series concept. All twelve singles charted in the UK Top 30, and the project received critical acclaim, with NME describing it as "casually revolutionary and underhandedly unique."

The original twelve tracks were subsequently compiled into two albums: Hit Parade 1 (June 1992) containing the first six singles and Hit Parade 2 (January 1993) containing the final six. These collections were later re-released as a double CD in 2003 under the title The Hit Parade, and a 30th-anniversary reissue on double vinyl and double CD followed in 2022.
